description: A website about The earth jukebox.
summary: Earth Jukebox is an interactive web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 that bridges the gap between raw satellite telemetry and intuitive visual storytelling. Managed by you during the October 2026 global hackathon, the platform transforms complex NASA Earth observation datasets into dynamic visual map layers and interactive climate trend charts. Rather than presenting users with overwhelming spreadsheets or technical logs, Earth Jukebox allows visitors to explore planetary shifts, environmental metrics, and historical climate patterns through a clean, accessible web interface. Despite its musical name, the project is strictly a visual telemetry tool and contains no audio or music playback features—the "jukebox" concept instead refers to how seamlessly users can select, switch between, and play back different Earth data tracks across time and geography, making planetary science engaging and understandable for everyone.
details:
Project Overview

  • Project Name: Earth Jukebox (developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge)
  • Tagline / Core Concept: "Same Planet, Different Stories"— An AI-powered interactive platform that bridges NASA Earth observation telemetry, environmental changes, and planetary data.
  • Team Members:
    • Team Leader: Waiz Hossain Araf
    • Research Member: Nazmus saqib Nuraz

Core Mission & Objectives

  • Democratizing Earth Science: NASA's Earth Information Center gathers massive data streams tracking global temperatures, thermal shifts, and environmental crises. However, these are often locked behind dense graphics and complex charts, creating accessibility barriers for younger students, ordinary citizens, and visually impaired individuals.
  • Multi-Sensory Experience: Built to provide an inclusive educational ecosystem where users can explore planetary metrics through interactive mapping, data visualization, and climate trend analysis.

Key Features & Functionality

  1. Interactive Global Mapping & Telemetry:
    • Explore global layers through high-resolution satellite and topography views.
    • Selecting specific regions or countries displays live station telemetry (such as local temperatures and atmospheric conditions).
  2. Climate Trend Charts & Comparison Engine:
    • Features interactive monthly temperature trend charts plotting annual climate variations.
    • Allows side-by-side comparison of contrasting regions to evaluate different thermal zones.
  3. Earth Lab & Time Machine:
    • Integrates the Earth Pulse system and an interactive time machine mode that lets users seamlessly navigate across historical data (e.g., from 2005), present observations, and predictive climate modeling extending up to the year 2100.
  4. Gamified Classroom Modules:
    • Includes interactive quiz modules featuring multi-round challenges (such as geographic rounds) to boost student engagement and test environmental knowledge using real-world satellite coordinates.

Future Roadmap

  • Launching a cross-platform mobile application.
  • Integrating real-time AI-powered environmental sensors.
  • Partnering with global educational institutions and classrooms worldwide to bring multi-sensory climate tools to students.
